one_liner: An adult male with a history of B-cell lymphoma and a right lung mass underwent right thoracotomy, right lower lobectomy, and en bloc resection of the diaphragm and portion of the liver, and was transferred to the PACU stable and extubated.

problems.name: Right lung mass invading diaphragm and liver

key_findings.name: Right lower lobe lung mass
key_findings.interpretation: Mass arising from right lower lobe invading diaphragm and liver

procedures.name: Right thoracotomy and right lower lobectomy with en bloc resection of diaphragm and portion of liver
procedures.outcome: Completed successfully, hemostasis achieved, patient extubated and stable

course.narrative: A male patient with a history of B-cell lymphoma and suspected mesothelioma was brought to the operating room for a right thoracotomy. Intraoperatively, the mass was found to arise from the right lower lobe and invaded the right diaphragm and the dome of the liver. The patient successfully underwent a right lower lobectomy with en bloc resection of the involved diaphragm and a wedge resection of the liver portion. Hemostasis was achieved. A 10-flat JP drain and a 32 straight chest tube were placed. The patient tolerated the procedure well, was extubated in the operating room, and transferred to the PACU in stable condition.
